purpose: Phase 1B coordinator closure of the FACT-IDENTITY architecture while keeping corpus execution as implementation evidence and excluding authority claims that require ARCH.PROBE-CONTRACT.
scopeRule: The fact-identity ladder, byte grammar, transition protocol, anchor ownership, and deterministic budget semantics are the included v1 architecture. Third-party/untrusted imperative execution and an ambient-authority guarantee are not included features.

normalisationLadder.identityRule: level id, level version, language id, and language toolchain identity are framed identity inputs; levels are distinct facts
normalisationLadder.capabilityRule: Unsupported or restricted language/level combinations produce exact Coverage deficiencies; no silent approximation is permitted

canonicalBytes.preimageRule: fixed domain tag followed by length-framed level, language, language-version, and payload components
canonicalBytes.payloadRule: L0 payload is exact raw body-span bytes and is never tokenised; L1-L3 payloads are framed canonical kind/value token streams whose registry and transform rules are committed by levelVersion
canonicalBytes.sourceRule: body spans use half-open byte offsets over snapshot-owned bytes; Unicode and line-ending behavior are level-specific and explicit
canonicalBytes.collisionRule: same identity with different canonical bytes is a host defect

v1Architecture.transitionRule: Changing an existing level algorithm dual-emits old/new versions, requires explicit acceptance, and records a deterministic many-to-many group witness; absent witness yields INDETERMINATE and re-baselining.
v1Architecture.anchorRule: Rules propose typed anchors; the host resolves, validates, canonicalises, and mints the final fingerprint. A rule can still cause quality churn by omitting valid anchors.
v1Architecture.budgetRule: Only deterministic budgets define semantic outcomes. Exhaustion discards the entire rule partition unless complete-page continuation is explicitly contracted; wall clock is a host-safety backstop only.

excludes: claims that FactQuery or a process boundary denies ambient authority
v1Exclusions.narrowTruth: The API supplies facts only. Linked first-party code, if any, is accepted TCB code under dependency audit; that audit is an integrity control, not confinement.
v1Exclusions.productBinding: product-dispositions.v1.json chooses no ecosystem depth, a narrow contribution ontology, and no public rule-IR freeze for v1.

requiredLater: adversarial, versioned TypeScript and Rust corpora over significant layout, directives/comments, strings/regex/templates, Unicode, mixed line endings, macros/generated syntax, and local binding renames
two independent producers for FI-13 canonical-byte equality
negative controls that intentionally perturb framing, language version, span boundaries, directives, and transition witnesses
retained execution records before a capability cell or identity stability property is advertised as demonstrated
equivalent evidence plus an explicit product scope change before any Python or Go matrix row is admitted by a shipping product
implementationEvidence.freezeRule: The corpus contents and execution records are implementation/qualification evidence, not a remaining choice in the byte grammar. Missing results prohibit DISCHARGED/DEMONSTRATED claims but do not reopen the selected ladder or grammar.

findingDispositions.reasoning: Every unexecuted property is SPECIFIED, PARTIAL, or NOT DISCHARGED; implementable:true alone never discharges it.
findingDispositions.verification: check-fact-identity.py rejects DISCHARGED with IMPLEMENTABLE_UNEXECUTED evidence.

findingDispositions.reasoning: The supported-language set, capability matrix, positive fixtures, and fact-plane deficiency vocabulary are mechanically joined.
findingDispositions.verification: check-fact-identity.py rejects matrix/fixture desynchronisation and missing language rows.

findingDispositions.reasoning: The canonical preimage is domain-separated and length-framed with exact span, token, Unicode, line-ending, and language-version rules.
findingDispositions.verification: check-fact-identity.py rejects missing byte grammar, damaged construction, and unframed components.

findingDispositions.reasoning: The architecture retracts ambient-authority absence, treats linked first-party code as TCB, and excludes third-party/untrusted imperative rules from v1.
findingDispositions.verification: check-fact-identity.py rejects loss of the exclusion and the coordinator closure's product-boundary checks reject ecosystem/public-IR expansion.

findingDispositions.reasoning: Semantically risky cells are full-provisional/restricted for shipping; promotion requires the named corpora. Corpus execution is not replaced with a paper claim.
findingDispositions.verification: The binding matrix and fixtures agree, and the closure forbids treating corpus absence as demonstrated capability.

findingDispositions.reasoning: The many-to-many witness includes accepted old/new group identities, typed edges, occurrence anchors, cardinalities, and deterministic ordering.
findingDispositions.verification: check-fact-identity.py rejects an empty or under-specified witness minimum.

forbiddenInferences: SEAL-WITH-CHANGES does not mean cross-producer identity is DEMONSTRATED.
A declared golden-corpus requirement is not evidence that the corpus ran.
The Rule API's facts-only surface is not a runtime authority boundary.
Schema-additive level addition does not make an existing-level algorithm change custody-reversible.
A rule cannot mint a fingerprint, but it can influence stability through its valid anchor choices.

set.title: Body-hash normalisation ladder, canonical byte grammar, and transition policy
set.note: Phase 1B coordinator closure: SEAL-WITH-CHANGES for the L0-L3 ladder, framed byte grammar, transition witness, anchor ownership, and budgets. L0 hashes raw span bytes; L1-L3 use a version-committed canonical token registry. TypeScript/Rust corpora remain implementation evidence and all affected properties stay SPECIFIED until retained results exist. Third-party/untrusted imperative authority is excluded on ARCH.PROBE-CONTRACT.
nonBlockingResiduals: FI-CORPUS-EVIDENCE — TypeScript/Rust adversarial two-producer corpora are implementation/qualification evidence; affected properties stay SPECIFIED until retained results exist
FI-PARK-IMPERATIVE-AUTHORITY — third-party/untrusted imperative rules and runtime ambient-authority claims remain excluded on ARCH.PROBE-CONTRACT
implementationEvidencePending: Implementation must populate and execute FI-13 corpora before promoting identity stability or provisional language cells; this is not an architecture blocker.

claimRegisterPatch.dependencyRationale: The v1 FACT-IDENTITY scope excludes third-party/untrusted imperative execution and retracts the ambient-authority guarantee rather than relying on ARCH.PROBE-CONTRACT.

knownLimitations: No TypeScript/Rust cross-producer corpus execution record exists yet.
The four-language matrix is an architecture capability contract, not the v1 installed-language set; v1 admits TypeScript and Rust only.
Linked first-party native rules, if later used, remain TCB code rather than confined extensions.
The host cannot prevent a rule from omitting otherwise valid anchors; fingerprint churn remains a rule-quality signal.

sealRecommendation.note: Seal the ladder, framed byte grammar, transition protocol, anchor ownership, and budget semantics. Carry corpus execution as implementation evidence and imperative authority as an excluded parked feature.
sealRecommendation.consumerB: Implement the selected grammar and TypeScript/Rust corpora. Do not invent an alternate preimage, silently approximate unavailable levels, freeze a public rule IR, or admit untrusted imperative rules.
